title: Unity Compiler Errors on Linux
body:
I'm trying to open the project on Linux, and have followed all of the instructions in `README.MD` (Will required adjustments, of course). I can open the project, but I get the following compiler errors:

```
Library/PackageCache/com.meta.xr.mrutilitykit/Core/Scripts/MRUKNative.cs(59,8): error CS1029: #error: 'Unsupported platform'
Library/PackageCache/com.meta.xr.sdk.core/Scripts/Editor/OVRManagerEditor.cs(352,79): error CS0103: The name 'manager' does not exist in the current context
Library/PackageCache/com.meta.xr.sdk.core/Scripts/Editor/OVRManagerEditor.cs(353,171): error CS0103: The name 'manager' does not exist in the current context
Library/PackageCache/com.meta.xr.sdk.core/Scripts/Editor/OVRManagerEditor.cs(353,216): error CS0103: The name 'manager' does not exist in the current context
Library/PackageCache/com.meta.xr.sdk.core/Scripts/Editor/OVRManagerEditor.cs(354,169): error CS0103: The name 'manager' does not exist in the current context
Library/PackageCache/com.meta.xr.sdk.core/Scripts/Editor/OVRManagerEditor.cs(354,214): error CS0103: The name 'manager' does not exist in the current context
```

I tried removing `Library/PackageCache`, and all it did was add the following warning:
```
The following asset(s) located in immutable packages were unexpectedly altered. Making changes to immutable packages isn't recommended because the changes can be lost without any warning during Package Manager operations.
  Packages/com.meta.xr.sdk.audio/editor/MetaXRAcousticMaterialMappingEditor.cs
  Packages/com.meta.xr.sdk.audio/Runtime/scripts/MetaXRAcousticMaterialMapping.cs
```

I know that Linux support is not important at all, I was just wondering if anyone had any ideas for solving this. Thank you for this awesome piece of software!
author: crummyh

comments.body: C# is a .NET platform. .NET uses compiled dlls for dependencies. Linux uses another format which it has to be cross compiled for. Meta only supports Windows and MacOS with there SDKs

Found the issue! `manager` is created in a compiler *if* statement:
```
#if UNITY_EDITOR_WIN || UNITY_STANDALONE_WIN || UNITY_EDITOR_OSX || UNITY_STANDALONE_OSX || UNITY_ANDROID
```
Meta dosn't support linux. :confused:

title: Timestamp Synchronization with RoboRio
body: Adds NetworkTables timestamp synchronization in order to ensure quest timestamp is in sync with RoboRio FPGA time, improving smoothness and accuracy of pose fusion with wheel odometry and other sources.
author: Adam-Kolt

comments.body: @Adam-Kolt Can you rebase this on main to fix the merge conflicts?

Actually, looking more, I feel like this could be solved a much different way, that doesn't lose information.

On the timestamp entry, use getAtomic() instead of get(). That will get you both the timestamp of the quest frame, and also the server time as part of the TimestampedDouble returned from getAtomic(). You then can use that value instead, to get the exact result you're seeing, but without additionally losing what the quest timestamp was.

title: Add heartbeat & Prevent Zombies
body:
# Fix Quest-Robot Reconnection Problems I'm back again! Thanks for making this @juchong. Figured I was overdue for a contribution. ## Problem Solved This PR addresses the issue where QuestNav fails to reconnect when the roboRIO reboots. The connection would appear active but no data would transfer ("zombie connection"). ## Key Improvements
🔄 Heartbeat System Added bidirectional heartbeat mechanism to detect stale connections: - Quest sends counter values to robot, which echoes them back - After 3 consecutive failed heartbeats, forces reconnection - Implemented in `ManageHeartbeat()`, `SendHeartbeat()`, and `CheckHeartbeatResponse()`
⏱️ Connection Timeout Protection Added timeout monitoring for connection attempts: - Tracks when connection attempts start with `connectionAttemptStartTime` - Automatically resets stuck attempts after 10 seconds (configurable) - Prevents the system from getting trapped in a "connecting" state
🔄 Improved State Management Restructured connection handling: - Added centralized `ForceReconnection()` method - Improved connection state flags management - Enhanced error handling throughout network operations - Prevents multiple overlapping connection attempts
🔍 Cleaner LateUpdate Flow Improved main loop logic: 1. Check for timed-out connection attempts 2. Manage connections based on state 3. Run heartbeat system before normal operations Creates a reliable state machine that can recover from any failure condition.
## Robot-Side Requirements On the roboRIO, add this code to echo heartbeat values: ```java /** Subscriber for heartbeat requests */ private final DoubleSubscriber heartbeatRequestSub; /** Publisher for heartbeat responses */ private final DoublePublisher heartbeatResponsePub; /** Last processed heartbeat request ID */ private double lastProcessedHeartbeatId = 0; // Initialize in constructor or setup heartbeatRequestSub = nt4Table.getDoubleTopic("heartbeat/quest_to_robot").subscribe(0.0); heartbeatResponsePub = nt4Table.getDoubleTopic("heartbeat/robot_to_quest").publish(); /** Process heartbeat requests from Quest and respond with the same ID */ private void processHeartbeat() { double requestId = heartbeatRequestSub.get(); // Only respond to new requests to avoid flooding if (requestId > 0 && requestId != lastProcessedHeartbeatId) { heartbeatResponsePub.set(requestId); lastProcessedHeartbeatId = requestId; } } ``` Call `processHeartbeat()` regularly in robotPeriodic or a periodic task. ## Testing Verified reconnection works properly in sim, but haven't tested with a real robot yet. Pushing this now as Week 3 is about to start. Will be testing on our robot tomorrow. Let me know if any changes need to be made! This makes QuestNav significantly more resilient to connection disruptions without requiring user intervention. The Quest handles its own connection state instead of relying on the NT4 master to notify of disconnections or trusting that NT4 will always cleanly handle it.

title: More Robust Pose Resetting
body:
## Made the Quest nav code more reliable and easier to work with. Main changes:

* Completely rewrote the pose reset system 
  * Now takes [X, Y, Rotation] from `/questnav/resetpose` instead of raw position/euler arrays
  * Simpler to use - just send field coordinates instead of calculating Unity transforms on RIO
  * Handles FRC -> Unity coordinate conversion properly
  * Added retry logic when reading pose data
  * Moves coordinate math to Quest - less processing on RIO
* Added field boundary checks (16.54m x 8.02m) to catch invalid poses
* Added a ping command (3) to test connection
* Better logging throughout the code
* Added XML comments/docs to everything
* Proper try/catch blocks around risky operations

## Breaking Changes

* Robot code will need to be updated to use the new pose reset format
* Old `/questnav/init/position` and `/questnav/init/eulerAngles` topics are removed
* New topic `/questnav/resetpose` expects array: [field_x, field_y, rotation_degrees]
* Much easier to use - just send the field position you want rather than calculating Unity transforms

## Notes

* Tested with various field positions including corners, center, and multiple rotations - all working correctly
* I have an example of the robot-side implementation using AdvantageKit if anyone's interested
* Keeps track of reset state better - should prevent double resets

Not super familiar with C# development so let me know if I accidentally broke something and I'll fix it!

Let me know if you run into any issues!
